full_judgment:
The Petitioner Nazir Ahmed, proprietor of Messer's Barisal Aluminum Works for the purpose of the extension of his industry, needed the land measuring an area of 30 decimal of land from plot No.1083, 1088, 1089 of Mouza Char Banda Kotwali Police Station. Barisal referred to as the 'Case Land' which is government Non-AgricuRural Khas Land adjacent to the industry of the petitioner filed application to the Ministry of Industries to facilitate in getting the settlement of the said land. After necessary inquiry and recommendation the Ministry of Industries sent the matter to the Ministry of Land, who then by its letter dated 29.4.95 asked the Deputy Commissioner. Barisal to for a aid settlement proposal of the case land in favour of the Petitioner as per Clause ৩(ড) of the Government Notification dated 7th March 1995 published in the Official Gazette on 8.3.95 (Annexure-A). Accordingly settlement Case No.4 (XIII)/ KT/95-96 was stated in the office of the Assistant Commissioner (Land) Sadar for settlement of the case land. But in the meantime another settlement case being settlement case No.22 KT/71-72 filed by respondent No.6 Ayon Ali Howlader for settlement 116 decimals of land from plot No.1088 and settlement Case No.2I KT/71-72 filed by one Abdus Salam Munshi and others for settlement 102 decimals of land from plot No.1083 were started and pending along with other cases. On 18.10.94 vide Memo No.2068 (Annexure-C) the Deputy Commissioner. Barisal forwarded the settlement Case No.22 KT-71-72 along with other 9 cases to the respondent No.1 Ministry of Land for further decision. In the meantime by the order of the President, a notification was issued and published in the Official Gazette on 8.3.95 prescribing the Government Policy for settlement of the Government Khas land, Ministry of Land in reply to the letter dated 18.10.94. (Annexure-C) asked the Deputy Commissioner vide Meme No. ভূম/শা-৮/খাজব/৪০৪/৯৫/১০৪ নং dated 6.2.96 to take action as per paragraph 9 of the above settlement Policy of the Government (Annexure-D). The Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenu) Barisal vide his memo no.S.A.1093 dated 21.4.96 (Annexure-E) again sought decision of the Ministry of land regarding settlement in favour of respondent No.6, wherein the said Ministry replied to decide the matter as per the above stated rules of the government. Thereafter respondent No.5 Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenu) Barisal executed and registered lease deed in favour of respondent No.6 on 21.11.96 just ignoring the petitioners claim. Against whereof an application of the petitioner, Ministry of Land vide its memo No. ভূঃ মঃ শাঃ-৮/খাজব/৩৫৭/৯৪/৭৩২ dated 28.9.97 directed the Commissioner, Barisal Division to decide the illegality, if any caused in granting settlement in favour of the respondent No.6 consequently Revision Case No.6, consequently Revision Case No.83 of 1997 was started and by the order dated 23.11.97 Additional Divisional Commissioner rejected the said settlement cases being No.21 KT/71- 72 and 22 KT/71-72 against whereof respondent No.6 preferred an appeal to Land Appeal Board which was registered as Appeal No.5-62 of 1997 (Barisal). By the impugned judgment and order dated 5.4.2003 (Annexure-H) the Chairman, Land Appeal Board (respondent- No.2) allowed the appeal and set aside the order dated 23.11.97 of the Additional Divisional Commissioner. Being aggrieved by the said order passed filed an application on 7.5.2003 to review the said order dated 5.4.2003 under section 6 of the Land Appeal Board Act, 1989. By the another impugned judgment and order dated 4.6.2003 (Annexure-M) the Chairman of the Land Appeal Board, rejected the Review petition. 

 3. The respondent No.6 opposed the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition sworn on 2.7.05. It is stated in the affidavit-in-opposition that respondent No.6 Ayon Ali Howlader had taken pattan of the case land from Syed Hatem Ali in 1949 who has been running his grocery shop after constructing a tin shad with pucca floor thereon since then. Thereafter when the case land had been decided as Government Khas land he applied for taking settlement of the same and accordingly settlement case No: 22KT/71-72 was started. After complying with the necessary formalities the A.D.C. (Rev) has correctly executed and registered the deed of settlement of the case land on 21.11.96 in his favour. But on wrong notion Additional Divisional Commissioner rejected the said settlement case against who roof as per proper legal forum he went to the land Appeal Board with an appeal and the Chairman of the Land Appeal Board After proper appreciation of law and facts set aside the 4 said order as well as affirmed the same in review accordingly committed no illegality. 

 5. Mr. P.C. Guha, the learned Counsel appearing for the respondent No.6 in reply argues that as per Section 147(c) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act an appeal shall lie to the Board i.e. Land Appeal Board. When the order is made by the Commissioner of a Division as such there was no illegality in entertaining the appeal of the present case by the Land Appeal Board. The rule is therefore liable to the discharged as of merits no consideration.
